title: First arrangement, East St. Louis Toodledoo, and his mother's death
summary: Jones tells of his first arrangement for Danny Williams's big band, written while his father coped with the loss of his mother.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: But it was during that period at Kentucky State that you wrote the school song, is that right?
Had you -- was that the first time you'd done any writing? You hadn't mentioned any writing. When was the first time you started writing?
I'm going to start this with a joke.

Oh, who did you write that for, the Danny Williams band?
Uh-huh, because he had a big band, see. Tony only had eight pieces.
But he was more associated with Duke. But there were more horns with Danny Williams, you know?

Five brass. At that time that was a big band. Five brass and four reeds. Was it four reeds? I guess it was four reeds and the regular rhythm section. You know? And my father used to look at me, he'd say, "James, I sure hope you finish that arrangement, because you've been banging on the piano all night and all day, trying to get yourself together." You know, he didn't use those words. And my mother had just died a little before then, you know, and so the old man and I, we had an apartment together, a small apartment. And the only therapy -- the best therapy I had was that music. Because I was in shock. He was, too. But by him being a choir director and fiddle player and whatever, that got him off the ground.
So he could last, you know? Because they stayed together like that, you know.
